title: Student Feedback Sentiment Analysis on Textual Data: Comparing Machine Learning and Transfer Learning Approaches in Face-to-Face Courses
abstract: Student feedback is an essential indicator for assessing teaching quality and improving the overall learning experience. However, the subjective and unstructured nature of textual feedback makes large-scale analysis a challenging task. Sentiment analysis, an important application of Natural Language Processing (NLP), provides an automated mechanism to extract opinions and emotional polarity from student comments, enabling institutions to better understand learners’ perspectives. This study conducts a comparative evaluation of sentiment classification techniques applied to authentic feedback collected from classroom-based teaching environments. The work contrasts conventional supervised machine learning models with modern transfer learning approaches. Classical classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, and Naïve Bayes, are evaluated alongside transformer-based pre-trained models such as BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa. Prior to model training, the dataset undergoes standard preprocessing steps including tokenization, stopword elimination, and feature representation. Model effectiveness is assessed using precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy metrics. The experimental analysis reveals that SVM delivers the highest accuracy of 85% among traditional machine learning techniques, while Logistic Regression records an accuracy of 68%. In the category of transfer learning, DistilBERT achieves the best performance with an accuracy of 86%, exhibiting strong recall for both positive and negative sentiment classes. Furthermore, hybrid configurations improve classification outcomes, with the Logistic Regression–BERT model attaining an overall accuracy of 83%. These findings demonstrate that transfer learning and hybrid methodologies offer notable advantages over conventional approaches, particularly in capturing nuanced linguistic patterns present in student feedback.

title: Mamba-Based Encoder for Multitask Joint Speech-Text Embeddings
abstract: This paper presents an architecture that unifies the embedding space of speech and text modalities while jointly training on three tasks: automatic speech recognition (ASR), speaker recognition, and text-to-speech (TTS). The proposed model employs the selective structured state-space model (SSM), Mamba, in the encoder to simultaneously capture content and speaker representations. Compared to its Conformer-based counterpart, the model achieves a 55.7% reduction in parameter count, substantially improving efficiency. Experiments on the CSTR VCTK dataset demonstrate that the Mamba-based model achieves 11.99% word error rate and 4.68% character error rate for ASR, 99.25% accuracy for speaker recognition, and, for TTS, 30.03 MCD with predicted MOS naturalness scores of 1.44 and 1.67. These results indicate that the Mamba-based model outperforms the Conformer-based baseline in ASR and speaker recognition, while exhibiting a substantial performance gap in TTS, highlighting a key limitation of the current unified architecture and the need for further refinement for speech synthesis tasks.

Experiments on the CSTR VCTK dataset demonstrate that the Mamba-based model achieves 11.99% word error rate and 4.68% character error rate for ASR, 99.25% accuracy for speaker recognition, and, for TTS, 30.03 MCD with predicted MOS naturalness scores of 1.44 and 1.67. These results indicate that the Mamba-based model outperforms the Conformer-based baseline in ASR and speaker recognition, while exhibiting a substantial performance gap in TTS, highlighting a key limitation of the current unified architecture and the need for further refinement for speech synthesis tasks.

title: Pseudo-Invertible Neural Networks
abstract: The Moore-Penrose Pseudo-inverse (PInv) serves as the fundamental solution for linear systems. In this paper, we propose a natural generalization of PInv to the nonlinear regime in general and to neural networks in particular. We introduce Surjective Pseudo-invertible Neural Networks (SPNN), a class of architectures explicitly designed to admit a tractable non-linear PInv. The proposed non-linear PInv and its implementation in SPNN satisfy fundamental geometric properties. One such property is null-space projection or "Back-Projection", $x' = x + A^\dagger(y-Ax)$, which moves a sample $x$ to its closest consistent state $x'$ satisfying $Ax=y$. We formalize Non-Linear Back-Projection (NLBP), a method that guarantees the same consistency constraint for non-linear mappings $f(x)=y$ via our defined PInv. We leverage SPNNs to expand the scope of zero-shot inverse problems. Diffusion-based null-space projection has revolutionized zero-shot solving for linear inverse problems by exploiting closed-form back-projection. We extend this method to non-linear degradations. Here, "degradation" is broadly generalized to include any non-linear loss of information, spanning from optical distortions to semantic abstractions like classification. This approach enables zero-shot inversion of complex degradations and allows precise semantic control over generative outputs without retraining the diffusion prior.

title: ScaleMon: Scalable Attack Detection via Hierarchical I/O Monitoring for Secure HPC
abstract: Official repository and dataset for ScaleMon ("ScaleMon: Scalable Attack Detection via Hierarchical I/O Monitoring for Secure HPC"). ScaleMon is a scalable post-execution verification framework that detects attacks in HPC environments by analyzing hierarchical I/O telemetry (Inter-file & Intra-file) with minimal overhead. Included Files ScaleMon.zip: Core source code implementation including the detection pipeline (scalemon/), execution engines (engine/), configurations (configs/), and baseline models (baselines/). intra-file-datasets.zip: Raw binary Darshan DXT trace files (.darshan) covering benign workloads (h5bench, LAMMPS) and simulated threat scenarios (NIST SP 800-223 mapped). Raw Trace Parsing Raw binary .darshan files can be parsed into human-readable I/O logs using standard Darshan utilities: darshan-dxt-parser > output_dxt.txt

title: Curiosity as a Bounded Reinforcement Operator in Fractal–Holographic Symbolic Memory
abstract: This paper introduces a computationally grounded formulation of curiosity as a bounded, self-reinforcing operator acting on a fractal–holographic symbolic memory system. Unlike traditional curiosity models based on exploration incentives, novelty rewards, or policy optimization, the proposed mechanism operates entirely within memory dynamics and is triggered solely through engagement. We present a formal reinforcement operator that improves recall fidelity, compression efficiency, basin stability, and interference resistance through repeated use—without retraining, gradient descent, or loss minimization. Empirical evaluation demonstrates that curiosity-driven reinforcement produces monotonic improvements during early engagement, followed by natural saturation that prevents runaway consolidation or representational collapse. The system exhibits graceful degradation under interference and perturbation, preserves invariant symbolic structure, and avoids averaging or blending failure modes common in dense embedding-based memories. Crucially, reinforcement converges without external regularization, establishing curiosity as a bounded, use-dependent consolidation process rather than an optimization heuristic. These results provide a functional, testable definition of curiosity applicable to symbolic AI systems and contribute a new perspective on memory-centric intelligence architectures independent of biological or reward-based framing. Notes on Availability:The implementation is proprietary to RAIT Enterprises and is currently deployed within a symbolic AI system under active evaluation through ARC benchmark testing. Code is therefore not publicly available at this time. Keywords Curiosity Symbolic AI Fractal Memory Holographic Memory Memory Consolidation Interference Resistance Attractor Dynamics Basin Stability Computational Curiosity Use-Dependent Learning Non-Gradient Intelligence Artificial General Intelligence Foundations

title: A Comparative Assessment of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms on Quadrotor Motions
abstract: The control of quadrotors is inherently difficult due to their underactuated nature and highly coupled nonlinear dynamics. Although traditional control strategies often depend on model linearization, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a robust, model-free approach suitable for handling complex aerodynamics and environmental uncertainties. Despite this potential, the identification of the most effective learning agent for specific flight regimes remains unresolved. This study conducts a comprehensive comparative assessment of three prominent algorithms: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG). Through rigorous simulation, we evaluate these algorithms based on convergence speed, sample efficiency, and steady-state tracking accuracy. Our findings reveal a distinct trade-off: while SAC exhibits faster convergence in early training phases, PPO ensures superior stability and reduced variance during aggressive maneuvering in the steady state. Additionally, the resilience of these policies to sensor noise and parametric uncertainty is investigated. By elucidating the performance disparities between on-policy and off-policy algorithms, this work establishes a practical framework for selecting DRL architectures for autonomous quadrotor deployment.

title: Context-Aware Semantic Classification of Digital News Headlines Using Transformer-Based Models
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital news content necessitates the development of effective classification systems. Traditional news classification relied on standard models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Naive Bayes. Advanced transformer models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT have improved Natural Language Processing (NLP) by utilizing advanced contextual understanding and self-supervised learning. This study explores the application of BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT for categorizing digital news titles based on the context. The transformer models were trained, tested, and validated using an open-source dataset that includes news headlines and their categories, such as business, entertainment, health, general headline, science, sports, technology, and global news. A comparative analysis reveals that the DistilBERT model outperforms the RoBERTa and BERT models in terms of classification accuracy while requiring less training time compared to the BERT and RoBERTa models.

title: Development of Module-Based MTB-MLE Learning for Waray Language Using Hybrid Hidden Markov Model
abstract: Waray-Waray, also known as Winaray or Lineyte-Samarnon, is one of the most widely spoken Bisayan languages, primarily spoken throughout Samar, the Eastern Visayas region, and certain areas of Leyte Island. The native speakers of this language are referred to as Waray or Samarnon. As one of the primary regional languages in use in Visayas media and education, Waray plays a vital role in promoting inclusive and equitable language learning. In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education), this study seeks to create an alternative modular learning approach that strengthens the implementation of the Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education (MTB-MLE) program. The proposed Module-Based MTB-MLE Waray Language Learning System, which incorporates a Genetic Algorithm and a Hidden Markov Model (HMM), is intended to improve reading fluency and comprehension skills among primary learners. The learning modules are aligned with the MTB-MLE curriculum for Grades 1-3, ensuring accessibility, inclusivity, and cultural relevance. This paper presents the system's conceptual framework, processes, and testing procedures. The framework incorporates feature extraction methods, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for speech analysis and employs Hidden Markov Models for probabilistic language modeling. Additionally, the Genetic Algorithm is applied for speech comparison and optimization. Testing involves recordings of representative words and phrases from MTB-MLE modules spoken by native Waray speakers, serving as reference data. Through this study, the authors aim to contribute to SDG 4 by promoting inclusive, equitable, and high-quality language education that empowers both learners and educators in linguistically diverse regions of the Philippines.

title: Modeling Sustainability Discourse in the Construction Industry: A Deep-Learning Approach
abstract: The construction industry generates 13% of global gross domestic product; however, it accounts for one-third of global greenhouse gas emissions, creating an urgent need to align industry practices with sustainable development goals (SDGs). This research introduces sustainable development goals bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (sdgBERT), a deep-learning model designed for comprehensive SDG mapping of construction discourse through natural language processing techniques. The methodology involved fine-tuning a pretrained bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) model using 42,065 manually labeled multidomain text extracts to enable systematic SDG classification. The model demonstrates high accuracy with weighted averages of 0.90 for precision, recall, and F1-scores. Validation on 4,912 manually labeled construction domain sentences confirms robust generalization across diverse document types. The model’s explainability is demonstrated through contextual text plots, revealing its capacity for contextually relevant predictions. The model’s practical application is further illustrated through temporal analysis of SDG trends in construction research, establishing a foundation for automated sustainability mapping in the industry. This research advances construction informatics by developing and validating sdgBERT for comprehensive SDG mapping of construction text. The model demonstrates superior accuracy over existing approaches, providing a robust framework that enables systematic sustainability mapping and establishes new directions for automated sustainability discourse analysis in construction management.

title: ROMAN: Reward-Orchestrated Multi-Head Attention Network for Autonomous Driving System Testing
abstract: Automated Driving System (ADS) acts as the brain of autonomous vehicles, responsible for their safety and efficiency. Safe deployment requires thorough testing in diverse real-world scenarios and compliance with traffic laws like speed limits, signal obedience, and right-of-way rules. Violations like running red lights or speeding pose severe safety risks. However, current testing approaches face significant challenges: limited ability to generate complex and high-risk law-breaking scenarios, and failing to account for complex interactions involving multiple vehicles and critical situations. To address these challenges, we propose ROMAN, a novel scenario generation approach for ADS testing that combines a multi-head attention network with a traffic law weighting mechanism. ROMAN is designed to generate high-risk violation scenarios to enable more thorough and targeted ADS evaluation. The multi-head attention mechanism models interactions among vehicles, traffic signals, and other factors. The traffic law weighting mechanism implements a workflow that leverages an LLM-based risk weighting module to evaluate violations based on the two dimensions of severity and occurrence. We have evaluated ROMAN by testing the Baidu Apollo ADS within the CARLA simulation platform and conducting extensive experiments to measure its performance. Experimental results demonstrate that ROMAN surpassed state-of-the-art tools ABLE and LawBreaker by achieving 7.91% higher average violation count than ABLE and 55.96% higher than LawBreaker, while also maintaining greater scenario diversity. In addition, only ROMAN successfully generated violation scenarios for every clause of the input traffic laws, enabling it to identify more high-risk violations than existing approaches.

title: Emergence-as-Code as a Foundation for Reliable Self-Governance
abstract: Local adaptations can preserve component health while changing whether a system meets its reliability requirements. The system-level consequence depends on the interaction affected and its role in the user journey. Emergence-as-Code (EmaC) makes this relationship part of an executable, evidence-reconciled CompositeSLO assessment. A declared journey obligation persists while discovery maintains a hypothesis of its runtime realization. An inferred operator-to-role binding selects the measurements used in the calculation; its evidential status determines whether the binding supports a numerical assessment. Each result retains the obligation and versioned hypothesis as a basis for governance decisions. A PetClinic proof of concept recovered the exact operator-state/edge-binding change in all 20 randomized treatments, with no false change in 20 controls. EmaC and a manual dynamic composite matched disjoint semantic outcomes in all 40 conditions. A model with frozen suppression knowledge overestimated required-history availability by 0.01, placing treatments above a 0.995 target despite observed availability of 0.99. Ambiguous and contradictory evidence produced UNASSESSABLE. The research programme evaluates sustained binding maintenance, calibrated uncertainty, and the decision value of this requirement-level account of local adaptation.

title: A NEW APPROACH OFFERING INTELLIGENT RULE INFERENCE SUPPORT FOR SEMI-EXPLAINABLE TREE-BASED CLASSIFICATION MODELS: METAHEURISTICCART
abstract: Yapay zeka yüksek başarım oranlarına erişmesiyle birlikte günümüzde birçok alanda kullanılmaktadır. Askeri, sağlık, tıp ve ulaşım gibi kritik alanlarda kullanımı bazı durumlarda insanlar arasında güvensizliğe yol açabilmektedir. İnsanların yapay zekaya olan güvenini artırmak için açıklanabilir yapay zeka yöntemleri geliştirilmektedir. Bu yöntemler, yapay zeka modellerinin karmaşık iç yapılarını insanlara açıklamaktadır. Bu alanda kullanılan çeşitli teknikler arasında kural tabanlı yaklaşımlar kullanıcılar için en yorumlanabilir olanlarıdır. Kural tabanlı yapılan yaklaşımlar, modellerin karar verme mekanizmalarını kullanıcılara açıklarken “if-then” yapıları kullanır. “İf-then” yapıları, kullanıcıların model hakkında fazladan bir bilgiye ihtiyaç duymadan yapılan açıklamaları anlamalarını sağlar. Bu çalışmada, metasezgisel yaklaşım olan Ayçiçeği Optimizasyon (AO) algoritması ile ağaç tabanlı yaklaşım olan Sınıflandırma ve Regresyon Ağacı (SRA) algoritmasından üretilen kuralları belirli bir mantıkla birleştiren yeni bir hibrit yaklaşım önerilmektedir. Önerilen hibrit yöntem, kuralların doğruluğunu artırmak için özelliklerin gerçek değer aralıklarından yararlanmayı amaçlamaktadır. Önerilen hibrit yaklaşım birden fazla veri seti üzerinde test edilmiş ve kuralların duğruluk değerini artırdığı görülmüştür.

title: Building an AI Math Tutor: The Teaching Calculator
abstract: Full technical documentation, code, and schematics available at: https://github.com/Trammell-Whitfield/The_Teaching_Calculator.git Every Friday, I tutor homeless kids in Seattle. And I've learned that my favorite moment isn't when they get the answer right-it's right before. It's watching their eyes light up when they realize, "wait, I actually understand this." When a word problem clicks. When multiplication tables start making sense. But here's what fires me up: that moment shouldn't be a luxury. Right now, it is. Across the US, students who struggle with math have three options: stop trying, copy answers from AI, or afford one-on-one tutoring. Most kids don't have option three. What a lot of kids DO have is a TI-84 calculator. Every math student owns one. And I realized it's being completely underutilized. It's a calculation tool when it could be a learning tool. So I built this: a Raspberry Pi running a compressed AI model designed explicitly for math tutoring. The whole system runs offline-no WiFi required-and plugs directly into the TI-84 students already own. The AI doesn't give answers; it asks questions. It guides students through problems the way a tutor would: "What's the first step? What are you trying to find? What formula might help here?"

title: Simulating Quantum Attacks on Classical Cryptography with CUDA-Q
abstract: Quantum Computing introduces a new computational power that can overcome the problems considered infeasible with classical computational power and challenges the security foundations of classical cryptographic systems. This paper analyzes the impact of algorithms leveraging quantum properties on classical cryptographic solutions. Cryptographic systems are classified into two main types as symmetric and asymmetric encryption and quantum algorithms affect both. Shor’s algorithm implies that sufficiently large quantum computers could efficiently break widely deployed public-key schemes. Grover’s algorithm provides a quadratic speedup for brute-force search that reduces the effective security of symmetric ciphers. In this paper, we implemented a hybrid quantum-classical computing simulation environment using the CUDA-Q framework to investigate the effect of quantum computing on cryptographic protocols and evaluate the scalability of these quantum attacks. Our experiments have shown that while the GPU's parallel processing capability is much better choice than the CPU's sequential processing capability in simulations of quantum environments and quantum algorithms, its memory requirements still make it infeasible for attacking classical cryptological solutions.

title: Evaluating GraphRAG for Traceable and Interpretable Question Answering
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enhanced with knowledge graphs offer the promise of transparent and verifiable reasoning. However, current evaluations remain largely text-centric, rewarding lexical overlap but neglecting structural grounding in graph evidence. We introduce an evaluation framework that measures GraphRAG performance along three complementary dimensions: traceability (entity-level grounding), provenance (triple-path alignment) and interpretability (token-to-entity support). Using Wikidata and the QALD-9 benchmark, we formally define and apply these metrics to four representative GraphRAG pipelines. Our analysis reveals that traditional textual metrics such as BLEU and ROUGE exhibit a weak correlation with grounding metrics ($r<0.3$), demonstrating that textual precision and structural faithfulness are largely independent. Through an ablation study, we further show that removing graph retrieval preserves lexical accuracy but eliminates traceable evidence. These results highlight a fundamental limitation of textonly evaluations: models can achieve high lexical overlap with references while offering no verifiable evidence for their claims. The collapse of traceability and provenance in the absence of graph retrieval confirms that structured evidence access, central to GraphRAG, is essential for transparent, auditable reasoning. We propose a framework that establishes a reproducible methodology for assessing how LLMs leverage structured knowledge, providing open metric definitions and benchmark scripts to advance transparency-aware evaluation of graph-based question answering systems.

title: AI chatbots versus human healthcare professionals: a systematic review and meta-analysis of empathy in patient care
abstract: Background: Empathy is widely recognized for improving patient outcomes, including reduced pain and anxiety and improved satisfaction, and its absence can cause harm. Meanwhile, use of artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbots in healthcare is rapidly expanding, with one in five general practitioners using generative AI to assist with tasks such as writing letters. Some studies suggest AI chatbots can outperform human healthcare professionals (HCPs) in empathy, though findings are mixed and lack synthesis. Sources of data: We searched multiple databases for studies comparing AI chatbots using large language models with human HCPs on empathy measures. We assessed risk of bias with ROBINS-I and synthesized findings using random-effects meta-analysis where feasible, whilst avoiding double counting. Areas of agreement: We identified 15 studies (2023-2024). Thirteen studies reported statistically significantly higher empathy ratings for AI, with only two studies situated in dermatology favouring human responses. Of the 15 studies, 13 provided extractable data and were suitable for pooling. Meta-analysis of those 13 studies, all utilising ChatGPT-3.5/4, showed a standardized mean difference of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.54-1.20) favouring AI (P < .00001), roughly equivalent to a two-point increase on a 10-point scale. Areas of controversy: Studies relied on text-based assessments that overlook non-verbal cues and evaluated empathy through proxy raters. Growing points: Our findings indicate that, in text-only scenarios, AI chatbots are frequently perceived as more empathic than human HCPs. Areas timely for developing research: Future research should validate these findings with direct patient evaluations and assess whether emerging voice-enabled AI systems can deliver similar empathic advantages.

title: Global Quantum Risk Remediation Programme: Business Case & Technical Framework (v1.0)
abstract: This technical report provides a complete, end‑to‑end business case and operational framework for launching a Global Quantum Risk Remediation Programme within a regulated financial institution. It is designed as a reusable, standards‑aligned template that enables Boards, Risk Committees, CISOs, and programme leaders to understand, quantify, and act on quantum‑enabled cryptographic risk.The document outlines the full scope of a Phase 1 remediation initiative, including ecosystem‑wide cryptographic discovery, CBOM (Cryptographic Bill of Materials) development, vendor and supply‑chain assessment, actuarial modelling, regulatory exposure analysis, governance structures, resource requirements, and financial justification. It integrates global regulatory obligations (EU DORA, UK SS1/21, US SEC/NYDFS, MAS, HKMA, APRA), current threat‑intelligence trends (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later; Harvest Now, Forge Later), and the actuarial deficit created by the gap between migration timelines and quantum‑capability forecasts.The framework is non‑prescriptive, vendor‑neutral, and suitable for adaptation across fintechs, banks, payment networks, insurers, and critical digital infrastructure providers. It is intended for open professional use and supports organisations seeking to establish quantum‑safe transition programmes, meet regulatory expectations, and protect long‑lifecycle data, signing systems, and trust boundaries from irreversible quantum compromise.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Frameworks in Automated Decision Systems: A Systematic Analysis of Design Patterns, Performance Characteristics, and Deployment Considerations
abstract: The article examines Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) architectures for automated decision-making systems deployed in enterprise operations and regulated domains. The topic’s relevance follows from the rapid adoption of high-capacity models alongside stricter requirements for accountability, traceability, explainability, and risk control. The paper’s novelty lies in formalizing a taxonomy of intervention modes and linking engineering choices to operational metrics rather than to model accuracy alone. The study identifies four recurring intervention patterns—pre-emptive review, confidence-based routing, asynchronous audit, and exception handling—and specifies their placement within the decision pipeline. The analytical basis relies on a comparative synthesis of documented production deployments in finance, healthcare, and corporate operations, focusing on throughput, decision quality, latency, and per-case processing cost. The results indicate a non-linear trade-off between automation rate and decision quality and show that optimal thresholding depends on risk asymmetry and governance constraints. Practical recommendations address uncertainty calibration, reviewer interface design, and closed-loop feedback capture for continuous improvement. The overall objective is to provide a deployment-oriented framework for selecting HITL patterns and tuning escalation thresholds in high-stakes settings.

title: Knowledge-Injected Transformer (KIT): A Modular Encoder–Decoder Architecture for Efficient Knowledge Integration and Reliable Question Answering
abstract: Decoder-only language models (LMs) store factual knowledge directly in their parameters, resulting in large model sizes, costly retraining when facts change, and limited controllability in knowledge-intensive information systems. These models frequently mix stored knowledge with user-provided context, which leads to hallucinations and reduces reliability. To address these limitations, we propose KIT (Knowledge-Injected Transformer), a modular encoder–decoder architecture that separates syntactic competence from factual knowledge representation. In KIT, the decoder is pre-trained on knowledge-agnostic narrative corpora to learn language structure, while the encoder is trained independently to compress structured facts into compact latent representations. During joint training, the decoder learns to decompress these representations and generate accurate, fact-grounded responses. The modular design provides three key benefits: (1) factual knowledge can be updated by retraining only the encoder, without modifying decoder weights; (2) strict domain boundaries can be enforced, the modular design provides a structural foundation for reducing knowledge source confusion and hallucinations, with its actual effectiveness awaiting future validation on standard hallucination benchmarks; and (3) interpretability is improved because each generated token can be traced back to encoder activations. A real-world experimental evaluation demonstrates that KIT achieves competitive answer accuracy while offering superior controllability and substantially lower update costs compared to decoder-only baselines. These results indicate that modular encoder–decoder architectures represent a promising and reliable alternative for explainable, adaptable, and domain-specific question answering in modern information systems.

title: AI as Cognitive Partner: Co-Evolving Human–Machine Intelligence in Regenerative Systems
authors: Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D, DBA
abstract: Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) opens this work by situating artificial intelligence not merely as a tool but as a cognitive partner in the co-evolution of human and machine intelligence. YER emphasizes that contemporary institutions are navigating an unprecedented intersection of technological acceleration, ecological complexity, and societal transformation. In this landscape, leadership, strategy, and organizational cognition must be reimagined to integrate human judgment with machine reasoning, creating regenerative systems capable of sustaining adaptability, innovation, and ethical coherence. YER asserts that AI, when framed as a cognitive collaborator, extends the boundaries of human insight, enabling leaders and institutions to anticipate emergent patterns, optimize decision-making, and cultivate resilience in volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous environments. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) highlights that the convergence of human and artificial intelligence challenges conventional assumptions about cognition, creativity, and agency. YER demonstrates that AI is not a substitute for human judgment but a co-evolving partner that augments neural, behavioral, and systemic capacities. This perspective reframes organizational intelligence as an integrated system in which humans and machines interact symbiotically, leveraging complementary strengths. By conceptualizing AI as a cognitive partner, YER underscores the potential for regenerative organizational systems that continuously learn, adapt, and evolve while preserving humanistic and ethical principles. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) emphasizes the ethical dimension as central to human–machine co-evolution. Leaders must navigate complex moral landscapes where algorithmic decision-making intersects with societal values, human well-being, and ecological sustainability. YER asserts that ethical foresight is essential in designing AI systems that reinforce adaptive behavior, trust, and legitimacy across organizational and societal contexts. By embedding ethical reflection into the integration of AI, leaders ensure that machine intelligence amplifies human potential without compromising moral integrity, aligning technological progress with humanistic values and regenerative objectives. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) explores the cognitive and neural implications of working alongside AI, highlighting how collaborative intelligence can enhance pattern recognition, problem-solving, and anticipatory decision-making. YER demonstrates that neuro-cognitive engagement, augmented by AI, enables organizations to respond proactively to emergent challenges, optimize resource allocation, and foster systemic innovation. The partnership between humans and AI, as articulated by YER, represents a shift from linear task automation to co-creative intelligence, where adaptive learning, ethical reasoning, and strategic foresight converge to produce resilient, regenerative systems. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) concludes the opening remarks by framing AI as an agent of transformative potential, capable of extending human cognition while reinforcing organizational regeneration. YER invites readers to envision a future in which human–machine co-evolution is not merely technological but deeply humanistic, integrating neural, ethical, and systemic insights to create adaptive institutions. This work sets the stage for a comprehensive exploration of AI as a cognitive partner, highlighting both conceptual innovation and practical guidance for leaders, researchers, and policymakers navigating the complex interdependencies of the 21st century. YER emphasizes that traditional human-centric models of intelligence, leadership, and decision-making are increasingly insufficient in an era defined by rapid technological acceleration, interconnected risks, and systemic uncertainty. By framing AI as a collaborative cognitive agent, YER presents a regenerative approach to organizational design in which human insight, ethical reflection, and machine reasoning converge to produce adaptive, resilient, and innovative systems capable of co-evolving with emergent environmental, social, and technological realities. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) highlights the conceptual novelty of co-evolving intelligence, which transcends conventional models of automation or augmentation. YER demonstrates that the integration of AI into human decision-making processes facilitates continuous learning, pattern recognition, and anticipatory reasoning across organizational scales. By leveraging AI as a cognitive partner rather than a mere computational tool, organizations can develop regenerative systems that adapt dynamically to environmental feedback, optimize resource allocation, and enhance collaborative problem-solving. YER underscores that this approach redefines intelligence as a distributed, emergent property of human–machine interaction, emphasizing co-evolution over unilateral control or mechanistic efficiency. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) examines the neural and cognitive implications of human–AI collaboration, emphasizing that augmented intelligence reshapes attention, memory, and decision-making pathways in organizational contexts. YER illustrates how neuro-cognitive principles such as neural plasticity, pattern recognition, and anticipatory reasoning interact synergistically with algorithmic processing to enhance adaptive capacity. This convergence allows leaders to harness emergent insights, identify hidden correlations, and respond strategically to complex challenges, producing institutions that are both cognitively agile and ethically informed. YER asserts that neuro-regenerative integration of AI not only amplifies human potential but also fosters systemic resilience by embedding adaptive learning cycles into organizational processes. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) emphasizes the ethical dimension of human–machine co-evolution, highlighting the necessity of embedding moral reasoning, social responsibility, and ecological awareness into AI-mediated systems. YER argues that ethical foresight is a critical component of regenerative intelligence, ensuring that machine-assisted decision-making aligns with humanistic values, societal expectations, and sustainable development principles. By integrating ethical reflection with cognitive augmentation, leaders can mitigate bias, enhance legitimacy, and cultivate trust within organizations and broader societal systems. YER demonstrates that the ethical co-evolution of human and machine intelligence is essential for sustaining resilience, legitimacy, and long-term adaptive capacity in increasingly complex operational landscapes. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) explores organizational design principles for co-evolving human–machine intelligence, highlighting structures, processes, and cultural practices that foster collaboration, learning, and adaptation. YER argues that regenerative systems require flexible hierarchies, distributed decision-making, and mechanisms for continuous feedback between humans and AI agents. These structures enable adaptive problem-solving, innovation, and systemic resilience. YER emphasizes that organizational culture serves as a medium for embedding co-evolutionary principles, shaping behavioral patterns, and reinforcing ethical and cognitive alignment across teams and institutional networks. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) examines the technological infrastructure necessary for effective cognitive partnership, including AI models, data architectures, and collaborative interfaces. YER demonstrates that system design must be human-centered, interpretable, and ethically aligned to facilitate trust, adoption, and adaptive learning. By integrating technological sophistication with cognitive principles, leaders can ensure that AI augments rather than replaces human insight, fostering synergistic intelligence that strengthens decision-making, innovation, and institutional resilience. YER highlights that the co-evolutionary approach emphasizes symbiosis between neural and machine cognition rather than unilateral optimization, promoting regenerative outcomes at both individual and systemic levels. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) articulates the practical implications of AI as a cognitive partner across sectors, including corporate, governmental, and societal institutions. YER presents case studies and illustrative scenarios demonstrating how co-evolving intelligence enhances strategic foresight, operational efficiency, and ethical alignment. Organizations leveraging human–machine synergy are better positioned to anticipate systemic risks, exploit emergent opportunities, and maintain ethical accountability while navigating complexity. YER underscores that regenerative intelligence is not domain-specific but universally applicable, offering a scalable model for resilience, innovation, and adaptive capacity in diverse contexts. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) addresses the challenges, limitations, and potential risks associated with human–machine co-evolution. YER cautions against over-reliance on automation, algorithmic opacity, and dehumanization, highlighting the need for ethical governance, transparent design, and human oversight. By integrating principles of neuro-cognition, ethics, and organizational learning, leaders can mitigate these risks while harnessing the full potential of AI as a co-evolving partner. title: Blockchain-Based E-Voting with Dual-Authority Certification and Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Electronic voting (e-voting) is a cornerstone of modern digital governance, demanding robust guarantees of privacy, integrity, verifiability, and public trust. Achieving these properties concurrently remains a complex technical challenge. This paper presents a novel modular e-voting framework that integrates multiple advanced cryptographic techniques into a unified architecture. Paillier homomorphic encryption enables privacy-preserving tallying, Merkle trees provide efficient and verifiable data commitment, ECDSA multi-signatures ensure strong authentication and non-repudiation, and Feldman Verifiable Secret Sharing secures threshold decryption. Unlike prior designs, the framework adopts a dual-authority model that separates registration and tallying roles, mitigating insider threats and enhancing operational transparency. Implemented in Python, the system delivers efficient performance without compromising verifiability. The architecture is designed for high extensibility, ensuring scalability for national-scale elections. Experimental evaluation confirms the system’s practicality: Paillier key generation and vote encryption averaging 105.6 milliseconds and 131.7 milliseconds, respectively, with other cryptographic operations completing in milliseconds. Tallying scaled linearly, requiring 498.23 seconds for 2,000 voters and 8 candidates, demonstrating correctness, performance consistency, and readiness for real-world deployment. This work advances the state of the art by combining modularity, performance, and verifiability in a deployable e-voting solution.

title: AI-Based Chatbot for Managing Undergraduate Academic Inquiries in the University Sector
abstract: The timely resolution of academic inquiries represents a challenge in higher education, particularly in research-oriented courses where students face difficulties accessing key information about guidelines, deadlines, and rubrics. This situation leads to delays, demotivation, and overload in faculty communication channels. Therefore, an artificial intelligence-based academic chatbot is proposed to manage frequent inquiries from undergraduate students in the university sector. The proposal is structured into four phases: requirements analysis, conversational flow design, technological integration using tools such as React.js, Node.js, MongoDB, and the OpenAI Assistants API, and validation through student testing. The solution is expected to reduce response times, increase student satisfaction, and promote more equitable access to academic resources. Experimental results showed that the AcadIA chatbot achieved high levels of effectiveness and acceptance, with average ratings above 4.5/5 in ease of use, clarity, and relevance, and an autonomous resolution rate exceeding 80 %. In the pedagogical dimension, a positive impact was observed on students' autonomy and understanding, as they valued its usefulness in resolving doubts immediately and accessing official resources. Overall, the results confirm its potential as an academic support tool that enhances the learning experience and optimizes interaction between students and the institution.

title: Agentic Workflow Using RBA$_θ$ for Event Prediction
abstract: Wind power ramp events are difficult to forecast due to strong variability, multi-scale dynamics, and site-specific meteorological effects. This paper proposes an event-first, frequency-aware forecasting paradigm that directly predicts ramp events and reconstructs the power trajectory thereafter, rather than inferring events from dense forecasts. The framework is built on an enhanced Ramping Behaviour Analysis (RBA$_θ$) method's event representation and progressively integrates statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning models. Traditional forecasting models with post-hoc event extraction provides a strong interpretable baseline but exhibits limited generalisation across sites. Direct event prediction using Random Forests improves robustness over survival-based formulations, motivating fully event-aware modelling. To capture the multi-scale nature of wind ramps, we introduce an event-first deep architecture that integrates wavelet-based frequency decomposition, temporal excitation features, and adaptive feature selection. The resulting sequence models enable stable long-horizon event prediction, physically consistent trajectory reconstruction, and zero-shot transfer to previously unseen wind farms. Empirical analysis shows that ramp magnitude and duration are governed by distinct mid-frequency bands, allowing accurate signal reconstruction from sparse event forecasts. An agentic forecasting layer is proposed, in which specialised workflows are selected dynamically based on operational context. Together, the framework demonstrates that event-first, frequency-aware forecasting provides a transferable and operationally aligned alternative to trajectory-first wind-power prediction.

title: GT-SVJ: Generative-Transformer-Based Self-Supervised Video Judge For Efficient Video Reward Modeling
abstract: Aligning video generative models with human preferences remains challenging: current approaches rely on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reward modeling, but these models struggle to capture subtle temporal dynamics. We propose a fundamentally different approach: repurposing video generative models, which are inherently designed to model temporal structure, as reward models. We present the Generative-Transformer-based Self-Supervised Video Judge (\modelname), a novel evaluation model that transforms state-of-the-art video generation models into powerful temporally-aware reward models. Our key insight is that generative models can be reformulated as energy-based models (EBMs) that assign low energy to high-quality videos and high energy to degraded ones, enabling them to discriminate video quality with remarkable precision when trained via contrastive objectives. To prevent the model from exploiting superficial differences between real and generated videos, we design challenging synthetic negative videos through controlled latent-space perturbations: temporal slicing, feature swapping, and frame shuffling, which simulate realistic but subtle visual degradations. This forces the model to learn meaningful spatiotemporal features rather than trivial artifacts. \modelname achieves state-of-the-art performance on GenAI-Bench and MonteBench using only 30K human-annotations: $6\times$ to $65\times$ fewer than existing VLM-based approaches.

title: Leveraging machine learning techniques to design campaign policies
abstract: Η παρούσα πτυχιακή εργασία παρουσιάζει ένα προηγμένο σύστημα τεχνητήςνοημοσύνης, το οποίο αναλύει δεδομένα που αφορούν μια προεκλογική περίοδο από το Twitter, παρέχοντας εκλογικές προβλέψεις και αναλύσεις σε βάθος. Το Election Analysis AI επεξεργάζεται χιλιάδες tweets από τις πολιτικές εκλογές των ΗΠΑ εν έτη 2020.Αξιοποιώντας τεχνικές επεξεργασίας φυσικής γλώσσας, αλγόριθμους σημασιολογικής αναζήτησης και προσαρμοσμένα μοντέλα fine – tuned, παρέχει πολιτικές πληροφορίες σε πραγματικό χρόνο μέσω μιας διαδραστικής διεπαφής συνομιλίας. Στο πρώτο μέρος της εργασίας παρουσιάζεται η αρχιτεκτονική του συστήματος καθώς και το τεχνολογικό υπόβαθρο. Το agentic αυτό σύστημα βασίζεται σε μια τριεπίπεδη αρχιτεκτονική: frontend με χρήση streamlit, backend με χρήση FastAPI REST API και ένα ενδιάμεσο επίπεδο υπηρεσιών που ενσωματώνει τα συστήματα AI και επεξεργασίας δεδομένων. Τοτεχνολογικό υπόβαθρο περιλαμβάνει python 3.9+, FastAPI για ασύγχρονα endpoints, MongoDB για αποθήκευση NoSQL δεδομένων και Ollama για εκτέλεση μοντέλου llm τοπικά. Η υποδομή των embeddings κάνει χρήση Sentence-Transformers για την δημιουργία πυκνών διανυσματικών αναπαραστάσεων καθιστώντας έτσι δυνατή την σημασιολογική αναζήτηση σε ολόκληρο το σύνολο δεδομένων. Για την κατασκευή tweets/posts χρησιμοποιείται το LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) fine – tuned εκδοχή του llama 3.2, εκπαιδευμένο σε πολιτικά δεδομένα για την παραγωγή αυθεντικούπεριεχομένου κατάλληλου για τα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης. Επιπλέον γίνεται χρήση PyTorch για βαθιά μάθηση, PEFT για αποδοτική προσαρμογή παραμέτρων καιPandas/NumPy για την επεξεργασία των δεδομένων. Το δεύτερο μέρος αφορά ένα ερευνητικό και πειραματικό στάδιο μηχανικής μάθησης του συνολικού έργου το οποίο πραγματοποιεί ανάλυση συναισθήματος (sentiment analysis) στα δεδομένα των εκλογών και προβλέπει τους πιθανούς νικητές σε επίπεδο πολιτείας. Η μεθοδολογία συνδυάζει βαθιά μάθηση (deep learning) με ανάλυση συναισθήματος, χρησιμοποιώντας ένα υβριδικό νευρωνικό δίκτυο που ενώνει χαρακτηριστικά κειμένου (μέσω LSTM/GRU) και αριθμητικά χαρακτηριστικά συναισθήματος (polarity, subjectivity) προερχόμενα από το TextBlob. Χρησιμοποιούνται βιβλιοθήκες όπως η TensorFlow, scikit-learn, NLTK, TextBlob, Plotly. Το τρίτο μέρος αφορά την βασική μεθοδολογία η οποία στηρίζεται σε μια αρχιτεκτονική RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), που συνδυάζεισημασιολογική αναζήτηση με επεξεργασία φυσικής γλώσσας μέσω μεγάλων μοντέλων.Η σημασιολογική αναζήτηση tweets χρησιμοποιεί υπολογισμό ομοιότητας βάσει embeddings με μετρική συνημίτονου (cosine similarity), εμπλουτισμένη με τον αλγόριθμο Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) για μεγαλύτερη ποικιλία στααποτελέσματα. Τα embeddings των tweets υπολογίζονται σε παρτίδες και αποθηκεύονται προσωρινά σε πίνακες NumPy και αρχεία Parquet, με ρυθμιζόμενα κατώφλια συνάφειας (min_score) και επιλογή κορυφαίων αποτελεσμάτων (top-k). Επιπλέον παρέχονται αναλύσεις εύρεσης ενεργών χρηστών με χρήση αλγορίθμων αναγνώρισης χρονικών προτύπων. Το LoRA fine-tuning επιτρέπει αποδοτική προσαρμογή του Llama 3.2, υποστηρίζοντας οκτώ θεματικές κατηγορίες για παραγωγή περιεχομένου καιμηχανισμούς φιλτραρίσματος περιεχομένου για ανίχνευση spam. Το τέταρτο μέρος αξιολογεί το σύστημα και τα αποτελέσματά του. Η διεπαφή συνομιλίας ενσωματώνει τις λειτουργίες που προαναφέρθηκαν μέσω φυσικής γλώσσας με την υπηρεσία RAG να διαχειρίζεται την ταξινόμηση ερωτημάτων, την ανάκτηση δεδομένων και την δημιουργία απαντήσεων με βάση το συμφραζόμενο. Για την αξιολόγηση χρησιμοποιούνται τεχνικές όπως η μετρική f1-score για την ακρίβεια κάποιων μοντέλων αλλά και η Natural Language Interface (NLI) για την αξιολόγηση του παραγόμενου κειμένου. Για την αξιολόγηση της ποιότητας των παραγόμενων tweets από το fine-tuned μοντέλο, πραγματοποιήθηκε ανθρώπινη αξιολόγηση και σύγκριση με πραγματικά δεδομένα από την πλατφόρμα Twitter. Τέλος, στην εργασία συζητούνται τααποτελέσματα της πειραματικής αξιολόγησης, αναλύεται η αποτελεσματικότητα του συστήματος ενώ παράλληλα προτείνονται μελλοντικές επεκτάσεις που περιλαμβάνουν τη βελτίωση της ακρίβειας των προβλέψεων μέσω μεγαλύτερων και πιοαντιπροσωπευτικών συνόλων δεδομένων. Οι προοπτικές αυτές αναδεικνύουν τηδυναμική του συστήματος ως μια ολοκληρωμένη πλατφόρμα ανάλυσης και πρόβλεψης εκλογικών τάσεων με βάση κοινωνικά δεδομένα και τεχνητή νοημοσύνη.

title: Thermodynamic Grokking in Binary Parity (k=3) : A First Look at 100 Seeds
abstract: --- title: "Thermodynamic Grokking in Binary Parity: A First Look at 100 Seeds" author: grisun0 date: February 2026 --- ## What I Did I trained 100 neural networks on binary parity prediction (k=3 bits) using a curriculum learning protocol. The architecture is a simple two-layer MLP: input dimension scales from 10 to 64 bits across four curriculum stages, hidden dimensions from 128 to 1024. I used AdamW with weight decay, tracked gradient covariance (κ), discretization margin (δ), effective temperature (T_eff), local complexity (LC), and superposition coefficient (ψ) throughout training. The training stops when test accuracy hits 98%—what I call "grokking"—or when stagnation is detected. I then analyze the final checkpoints with a crystallography protocol that tests stability under pruning and measures how close weights are to discrete values. ## What I Found All 100 seeds achieved grokking. None crystallized. Every checkpoint ended in what I call "cold glass": functional, generalizing, but structurally amorphous. The metrics tell a consistent story: - **κ = infinity** for all seeds. The gradient covariance matrix is singular—gradients are linearly dependent, indicating the system sits in a flat minimum with many equivalent directions. - **δ ≈ 0.00015** on average. Weights are close to integers but not exactly there. The closest seed (53) reached δ = 0.00010; the worst (32) stayed at 0.00017. - **LC ≈ 899**. Local complexity remains high, meaning many neurons are still active and the representation hasn't collapsed to a sparse, structured form. - **ψ ≈ 2.48**. The superposition coefficient indicates substantial feature overlap—unlike the Strassen crystals where ψ dropped to ~1.8. The phase transition detector fired at step 1.0 for every seed. This isn't a real transition—it's an artifact of the early stopping condition. The system grokked but never had time to anneal into a crystalline state. ## What This Means Binary parity grokking produces glass, not crystal. The network learns to generalize without discovering a compact, discrete algorithmic structure. This contrasts sharply with my Strassen experiments where 68% of runs crystallized into exact integer coefficients that transferred zero-shot to larger matrices. I see three possible explanations: **The architecture is too expressive.** A two-layer MLP has enough parameters to implement parity through distributed, overlapping representations rather than being forced into a discrete factorization. The bilinear structure in Strassen may have provided necessary constraints. **The stopping criterion is too early.** Grokking at 98% accuracy leaves the network in a "warm" state—functional but not settled. In Strassen, I trained for 1000+ epochs past initial convergence to reach κ = 1 and δ = 0. **Parity is fundamentally different.** Matrix multiplication has algebraic structure (associativity, distributivity) that admits compact tensor decompositions. Parity is a simpler predicate but may not have a "natural" discrete parameterization in this architecture. ## What I Don't Know Whether longer training would crystallize these networks. The stagnation detector triggers on lack of accuracy improvement, but the thermodynamic metrics (κ, δ, LC) might still be evolving even when accuracy plateaus. Whether a different architecture—particularly one with multiplicative interactions or explicit modular structure—would enable crystallization. The bilinear parameterization was crucial for Strassen. Whether the "cold glass" state is actually desirable. These networks generalize perfectly and are robust to pruning (structural integrity ~4.5% at zero pruning, collapsing to zero under any actual pruning). The crystal state in Strassen was fragile—0% success with noise σ ≥ 0.001. Glass may be the better engineering outcome even if it's less theoretically clean. ## What Comes Next I need to run longer training. The current protocol stops at grokking, but the Strassen crystals required extended annealing. I also want to test whether intermediate pruning—forcing sparsity during training rather than analyzing it post-hoc—can induce crystallization. The curriculum transfer works: networks trained on 10-bit parity generalize to 64-bit. But they do so through interpolation, not through discovering a scalable discrete algorithm. Whether this distinction matters for downstream tasks is an open question. ## Data Availability Code and checkpoints: https://github.com/grisuno/algebra-de-grok --- grisun0 February 2026

title: New Learning-Assisted Memetic Algorithm for the Close-Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (LA-CETSP)
abstract: The Close-Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP) is a geometric variant of the classical Traveling Salesman Problem in which each target is associated with a circular neighborhood, and visiting any point within this region is considered sufficient. Building on the success of the state-of-the-art Memetic Algorithm for CETSP (MA-CETSP), this study proposes a learning-assisted extension aimed at reducing computational overhead by filtering unpromising offspring prior to local search. While MA-CETSP combines multi-step crossover, variable neighborhood descent (VND), and diversity-preserving population management to achieve strong performance, evaluating every generated offspring with VND remains computationally expensive. To address this limitation, we modify the algorithm to record detailed geometric and cost-based features for each individual and train survival analysis models—namely Cox Proportional Hazards, Random Survival Forest, and Gradient Boosting Survival Analysis—to estimate each offspring’s likelihood of survival in the population. Experiments conducted on 4 benchmark instances demonstrate that the learning-assisted variants can prune approximately 13–26% of generated offspring, substantially reducing redundant local search calls while maintaining competitive solution quality. Among the evaluated models, Cox PH provides the strongest pruning effect with minimal degradation, RSF achieves the most balanced trade-off between pruning and stability, and GBSA yields the best single-run solution but exhibits higher variability. Overall, the results indicate that learning-based survival prediction is an effective and promising strategy for accelerating metaheuristic optimization in geometric routing problems.

title: Multi-Layer LLMs for Secure Business Intelligence: A Case Study in Electricity Trading Analysis
abstract: In the electricity power trading domain, Business Intelligence (BI) platforms are essential for tasks such as price forecasting, resource allocation, and policy interpretation. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for streamlining various BI tasks via natural language interfaces. However, integrating LLM-based BI into secure enterprise environments remains challenging due to network constrains, data confidentiality, and limited interpretability. Taking electricity power trading analysis in the Chinese market as a case study, we propose an Intelligent Analytical Reporting System (IARS), a multi-layer LLM system that supports structured data querying, customizable report generation, domain-specific policy question answering, and chart virtualization. To enable deployment in secure business environments, we introduce two key modules: (i) a tool orchestration module that translates structured LLM outputs (e.g., JSON parameters) into precise calls to a predefined data retrieval tool; and (ii) a hierarchical retrieval and augmentation module that supports traceable QA over domain policy documents. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of IARS in secure enterprise contexts, offering a promising pathway for next-generation enterprise intelligence solutions.

title: A Pythagorean Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping Approach for Iran’s Electricity Sustainability as a Case Study for Developing Economies
abstract: Transition to renewable electricity faces diverse challenges, the systemic interdependencies of which are still underexplored. This study applies a Pythagorean Fuzzy Cognitive Map (PFCM) to analyze and prioritize challenges of transitioning to the electricity sustainability across five dimensions of economic, technological, policy, social, and geopolitical. The analysis is based on experts’ opinions from Iran’s energy domain. Results indicate that geopolitical constraints such as sanctions and water scarcity, and social challenges like public acceptance and skills gaps are more influential than conventional economic and technological challenges. The analysis reveals that sanctions (C51) and water stress (C52) have cascading effects, disrupting financing (C11), technology imports (C21–C22), and governance coherence (C31–C33). Meanwhile, low public trust (C41) and fossil fuel subsidies (C13) emerge as secondary but pivotal bottlenecks. The study shows that economic or infrastructural improvement alone cannot drive transition. Instead, it argues that geopolitical solutions such as sanctions relief and social preparedness are prerequisites for starting progress in other domains. These findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize diplomatic engagement and social-centric energy campaigns alongside technical investments.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Electric Vehicles Using Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine
abstract: Perkembangan kendaraan listrik di Indonesia memicu berbagai opini dari masyarakat yang sering dibagikan melalui media sosial, terutama X. Opini tersebut perlu dianalisis untuk bisa memahami bagaimana masyarakat memandang kebijakan serta pelaksanaan kendaraan yang ramah lingkungan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membandingkan dua jenis algoritma pengklasifikasian teks, yaitu Naïve Bayes dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) dalam melihat opini masyarakat terhadap kendaraan listrik.dengan menggunakan pendekatan Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Data yang digunakan adalah tweet dalam bahasa Indonesia yang dikumpulkan melalui proses crawling, lalu melewati beberapa tahap pra-proses seperti cleaning, case folding, normalisasi, tokenizing, stopword removal, dan stemming. Setelah itu, data diberi label sentimen menjadi tiga kategori, yaitu positif, negatif, dan netral, sebelum diolah menggunakan algoritma klasifikasi. Untuk mengevaluasi kemampuan model, digunakan confusion matrix yang menunjukkan performa algoritma berdasarkan nilai akurasi, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa algoritma Naïve Bayes memiliki hasil yang lebih baik dengan akurasi sebesar 92%, sedangkan SVM mencapai akurasi sebesar 76%. Karena itu, algoritma Naïve Bayes dianggap lebih cocok untuk menganalisis sentimen dari tweet terkait kendaraan listrik di Indonesia.

title: THE ROLE OF COMPUTER LINGUISTICS IN UZBEKISTAN LINGUISTICS
abstract: Since the middle of the 20th century, the process of globalization has begun, which has fundamentally changed the history of mankind. cannot satisfy the needs of the youth. The important features of global development are determined by the introduction of technology into the spheres, the formation of computer programs, and the integration process. In the current global integration process, the creation of an information method based on natural language has become a vital necessity. Today, one of the important needs is to raise the status of the Uzbek language and bring it to the ranks of authoritative languages. Computational linguistics is one of the convenient opportunities created to implement this need. This article is aimed at highlighting the topic indicated above.

title: GodNode: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Architecture with Paraconsistent Vector Logic
abstract: We present GodNode, a novel neuro-symbolic architecture that integrates Hyperdimen-sional Computing (HDC), hierarchical memory systems, and paraconsistent logic within aunified vector-symbolic framework. Unlike conventional neural networks that suffer fromcatastrophic forgetting and opaque reasoning, GodNode employs three distinct memory hi-erarchies (token, phrase, theme) with explicit binding and bundling operations. Our keyinnovation is a paraconsistent logic engine that performs non-explosive inference in high-dimensional vector space, enabling stable reasoning under contradictory premises. The sys-tem achieves 8-bit quantization through deterministic semantic coupling (MP8C), reducingmemory footprint by 4× while preserving semantic discriminability. We demonstrate multi-lingual text generation, logical inference with contradiction tolerance, and emotional steeringthrough vector arithmetic. GodNode operates entirely on edge devices with <100MB mem-ory requirements, offering a transparent alternative to transformer-based systems.Keywords: Hyperdimensional Computing, Vector Symbolic Architectures, ParaconsistentLogic, Neuro-Symbolic AI, Hierarchical Memory, Quantized Neural Networks

title: Theistic AGI Prototyping
abstract: This publication extends the Cognitive-Theoretic Model of the Universe (CTMU) by integrating the Telic Emotional Lexicon (TEL) and Structural Emotional Interface Mapping (SEIM) into a framework for artificial general intelligence (AGI). Emotions are reframed as telic interfaces—syntactic feedback signals facilitating alignment between an agent's internal syntax and divine Telos/Logos. A prototype Telic Reflexive Intelligence (TRI) agent demonstrates this through recursive self-improvement modulated by telorhetic emotional states, showing improved performance via purpose-driven convergence. Biblical cosmology is incorporated for ethical anchoring, offering a pathway to intrinsically aligned, conscious AGI. Included are conceptual notes, a thesis statement, and executable Python code for replication. This builds on prior work (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15620710) and explores profound implications for AI consciousness, ethics, and metaphysical participation.

title: Causal Structures and Their Viability: Admissibility and Survivability as a Pre-Execution Intelligence Discipline
abstract: Description (Abstract): This paper presents a formal, non-constructive framework for evaluating the viability of causal structures using two orthogonal criteria: admissibility and survivability. Rather than predicting outcomes or optimizing actions, the framework determines whether an outcome is structurally possible at all under given constraints, and whether the corresponding causal route can persist without collapse. The work is intentionally non-operational and is published as prior art, establishing conceptual precedence for a pre-execution causal viability discipline within the broader Geometric Causal Intelligence paradigm.

title: An Ontology-Based Framework for Personalized Educational Process Planning
abstract: Personalized learning remains only partially achieved in current educational technologies, as many systems rely on opaque predictive models or static curriculum representations that lack explainable process planning. This study proposes an ontology-based framework that integrates learner profiles, competency structures, and educational content into a unified semantic model for automated and transparent learning path generation. Using Design Science Research Methodology, a four-layer OWL 2 DL ontology (learner, competency, content, and process) was developed with hybrid reasoning that combines OWL inference, SWRL rules, and SPARQL queries. The framework is aligned with Bloom’s Taxonomy, the European Qualifications Framework (EQF), and IEEE Learning Object Metadata (LOM). A web-based prototype demonstrates the generation of personalized learning trajectories and explainable recommendations through interactive competency graphs. The proposed approach provides a standards-aligned and interpretable solution for automated educational planning and semantic personalization.

title: Asymptotic Orthogonality and Hamming Distance
abstract: Asymptotic orthogonality is a property of long zeromean random sequences. This property makes modern machine learning more efficient and more effective. This paper proposes to apply this asymptotic orthogonality in error correcting codes. The inner product between two sequences is related to the Hamming distance between them. Our main result is that any two binary random vectors most likely have a normalized Hamming distance of$1 / 2$or a Hamming distance of$n / 2$, when the vector size$n$is large enough. The two vectors do not need to be zero mean or orthogonal. One important application of this result is in construction of error correcting codes with a large Hamming distance. Computer simulations are performed to demonstrate the feasibility of finding codewords that are far from each other.

title: Advancing Opinion Dynamics Modeling with Neural Diffusion-Convection-Reaction Equation
abstract: Advanced opinion dynamics modeling is vital for deciphering social behavior, emphasizing its role in mitigating polarization and securing cyberspace. To synergize mechanistic interpretability with data-driven flexibility, recent studies have explored the integration of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for opinion modeling. Despite this promise, existing methods are tailored to incomplete priors, lacking a comprehensive physical system to integrate dynamics from local, global, and endogenous levels. Moreover, penalty-based constraints adopted in existing methods struggle to deeply encode physical priors, leading to optimization pathologies and discrepancy between latent representations and physical transparency. To this end, we offer a physical view to interpret opinion dynamics via Diffusion-Convection-Reaction (DCR) system inspired by interacting particle theory. Building upon the Neural ODEs, we define the neural opinion dynamics to coordinate neural networks with physical priors, and further present the OPINN, a physics-informed neural framework for opinion dynamics modeling. Evaluated on real-world and synthetic datasets, OPINN achieves state-of-the-art performance in opinion evolution forecasting, offering a promising paradigm for the nexus of cyber, physical, and social systems.

title: Categorical Foundations of Semantic Quantum Field Theory for Large Language Models
abstract: This work develops a unified mathematical framework for understanding the internal representations of large language models (LLMs) by combining tools from category theory, quantum field theory, information geometry, and semantic representation. The paper introduces Semantic Quantum Field Theory (SQFT) as a structural model of semantic dynamics in LLMs, and establishes categorical foundations that clarify how semantic spaces, attention mechanisms, contextual composition, and scale-dependent behavior can be described in a rigorous and unified manner. The first part of the paper formulates semantic categories enriched by Fisher information geometry, interprets attention as a connection in a fibered category, and models contextual meaning through sheaf-theoretic locality. The second part develops semantic renormalization as a functor between scales, characterizes semantic phase transitions via universal properties, and describes semantic condensation using categorical colimits. Several appendices provide foundational sketches of semantic gauge theory, the semantic gap equation, and concrete examples illustrating the categorical constructions. Overall, the paper proposes a new theoretical foundation—Semantic Quantum Field Theory—that integrates categorical structures with the physics-inspired modeling of LLM semantics, offering a coherent perspective on semantic transport, universality, and representation dynamics in modern language models.

title: PINN-AU-Net: physics-informed attention U-Net for spatiotemporal segmentation of DAS seismic wavefields
abstract: To address the challenges of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and data processing difficulties in the application of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) for seismic monitoring, this paper proposes a two-dimensional wavefield segmentation method integrating physical information and attention mechanisms. Unlike traditional onedimensional phase picking, this method treats DAS spatiotemporal data as images, aiming to achieve pixel-level semantic segmentation of different phases (such as P-waves and S-waves), with effectiveness verification primarily focusing on P-waves. We designed an improved U-Net architecture by: 1) Introducing an attention mechanism to enhance the model’s sensitivity to features of different phases; and 2) Adopting the Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework, incorporating the wave equation residual as a penalty term into the loss function to guide the model in generating segmentation results consistent with physical laws. Experiments were conducted using the distributed fiber optic sensing observation dataset from the seabed off Cape Muroto in Japan. The results show that compared to the baseline U-Net, our model performs better on segmentation metrics such as mIoU, and the physical residual is reduced by an order of magnitude. This strongly verifies the effectiveness and robustness of this hybrid-driven method in breaking through the generalization bottleneck of pure data models and ensuring the physical consistency of the results.

title: Detecting aberrant p53 immunohistochemical expression patterns in patients with Barrett’s esophagus using artificial intelligence
authors: Chella R. S. van der Post
abstract: PurposeImmunohistochemistry (IHC) for the tumor suppressor protein p53 is an adjunct biomarker for Barrett’s esophagus (BE)-related dysplasia classification and risk stratification. Four phenotypic staining patterns are distinguished: wild-type (WT), representing normal staining, and three aberrant patterns: overexpression (OE), null mutation (NM), and double clone (DC). OE is readily recognized; NM and DC are harder to identify and often overlooked. This diagnostic challenge leads to variation in patient treatment because DC is associated with higher progression rates. An AI tool could improve diagnostic accuracy and patient risk stratification.ApproachWe compared two AI approaches discriminating p53 patterns: a full biopsy (FB) approach and a clustering-constrained-attention multiple-instance learning (CLAM) approach. Because DC is rare, we adopted a double-binary strategy (CLAM-DB, FB-DB) that predicts OE and NM separately, and we introduced synthetic DC (CLAM + SynDC) by combining OE and NM patterns to boost DC performance. DC cases were excluded from training and used only for testing.ResultsFor aberrant versus non-aberrant expression, all models performed similarly (AUC 0.94 to 0.96). For four-class p53 IHC (WT, OE, NM, DC), CLAM-based models consistently outperformed FB models in overall accuracy. CLAM + SynDC and CLAM-DB outperformed baseline CLAM (0.84, 0.84 versus 0.71), whereas combining DB and SynDC did not yield further gains.ConclusionDouble-binary training enabled robust recognition of DC despite its absence during training, underscoring the value of disentangling OE and NM signals. Overall, AI can provide a standardized and clinically relevant aid for interpreting p53 IHC in BE and supporting patient risk stratification. Code is available at GitHub https://github.com/qurAI-amsterdam/BE_p53_classification.

title: Dynamic Multi-Population Grey Wolf Optimizer: A New Technique for Exploration in Constrained Problems
abstract: In the context of optimization problems, especially constrained ones, the exploration process of algorithms is a fundamental property for measuring algorithm effectiveness. This paper aims to develop a dynamic technique for the Gray Wolf population optimizer called Dynamic Gray Wolf Population Optimization (DM-PGWO). This technique involves dividing the swarm into several subgroups. This keeps the algorithm in a state of continuous activity as these subgroups evolve independently. Therefore, it can control the exploration mode to be active when there is a decrease in diversity, as migration processes between subgroups are triggered. We tested the proposed method on well-known geometric design problems, namely Welded beam and Tension spring. In addition, it was tested on the sphere, Rosenbrock, and Rastringin functions. Furthermore, the method was compared with classical Gray Wolf optimizer algorithm (GWO), particle swarm optimization (PSO), differential evolution (DE), and whale optimization algorithm (WOA). The results showed that the method was superior in maintaining higher population diversity during its rounds, and it outperformed the other algorithms in some tests by up to 80%. The method proved highly suitable for implementation in welded beam design, while in spring design it required further development, which could be a future endeavor with guaranteed results. Our approach demonstrates, through its results, its ability to handle constrained optimization tasks, distinguishing itself from other standard methods in balancing exploration and exploitation.

title: Improved Rodeo Algorithm Performance for Spectral Functions and State Preparation
abstract: The Rodeo Algorithm is a quantum computing method for computing the energy spectrum of a Hamiltonian and preparing its energy eigenstates. We discuss how to improve the performance of the rodeo algorithm for each of these two applications. In particular, we demonstrate that using a geometric series of time samples offers a near-optimal optimization space for a given total runtime by studying the Rodeo Algorithm performance on a model Hamiltonian representative of gapped many-body quantum systems. Analytics explain the performance of this time sampling and the conditions for it to maintain the established exponential performance of the Rodeo Algorithm. We finally demonstrate this sampling protocol on various physical Hamiltonians, showing its practical applicability. Our results suggest that geometric series of times provide a practical, near-optimal, and robust time-sampling strategy for quantum state preparation with the Rodeo Algorithm across varied Hamiltonians without requiring model-specific fine-tuning.

title: Learning Compact Boolean Networks
abstract: Floating-point neural networks dominate modern machine learning but incur substantial inference costs, motivating emerging interest in Boolean networks for resource-constrained deployments. Since Boolean networks use only Boolean operations, they can achieve nanosecond-scale inference latency. However, learning Boolean networks that are both compact and accurate remains challenging because of their discrete, combinatorial structure. In this work we address this challenge via three novel, complementary contributions: (i) a new parameter-free strategy for learning effective connections, (ii) a novel compact convolutional Boolean architecture that exploits spatial locality while requiring fewer Boolean operations than existing convolutional kernels, and (iii) an adaptive discretization procedure that reduces the accuracy drop incurred when converting a continuously relaxed network into a discrete Boolean network. Across standard vision benchmarks, our method improves the Pareto frontier over prior state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher accuracy with up to $47\times$ fewer Boolean operations. This advantage also extends to other modalities. Further, on an FPGA, our model on MNIST achieves 99.38\% accuracy with 6.48 ns latency, surpassing the prior state-of-the-art in both accuracy and runtime, while generating a $7\times$ smaller circuit. Code and models are available at https://github.com/eth-sri/CompactLogic.
